Your Training

Summary of practice

1. Listen to the Being Right lesson audio

2. Write about the what the Judge feels it is “right” about. You might also write
about when the Judge rates “I” as smarter, superior, correct. Also write about what this
character says about others when they are wrong, stupid, or in some way inferior. This
is an indirect way to “feel right” and create a feeling of self worth, self-acceptance, or
self love.

3. Notice the emotions you create within yourself through the use of these
opinions about being right or superior. Write out what these emotions are and
how your characters create them using these stories. Can you get these emotions
through other expressions?



Some notes

This is an exploration of the Judge mechanism for creating good emotions. We want the
good emotions but how to get them without the problems beng “right” create. The good
feeling emotions are fine, but the way they are created is through a rejection, or
criticism of others, or ourselves. The rejection might be indirect, but it is embedded in
the superiority.

It might not be obvious that you are creating feelings of feeling good with self criticism
this way. It might be a layer or two deeper in the sub-conscious that the Image of
Perfection is residing. We will get to that later. It will likely be easier to notice the
thoughts of comparison to others that create “superiority”.

Complaining is a kind of superiority in action. A complaint has some superiority about
how things should have happened. I use the bridge example in the audio. If I can find
something wrong with what a customer service person did, or a meal, or movie, then the
Judge has indirectly pointed to the “self” being superior.

Obstacles you are likely to find

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-obstacles-you-are-likely-to-find-6431213

Giving up “being right” would also mean giving up the love and good feelings of our
emotions. When you work on giving up the stories and opinions of “being right” your
mind will not want to give up the good feelings that go with it. That’s understandable.

How can you have the good feelings, but without the story comparing you with another
person? How about revisiting the practices of Gratitude, Acceptance, Silent Mind, and
Meditation. You have ways to create those emotions and you don’t have to be
dependent on that characters story of superiority.

Giving up complaining, that’s likely to leave you a lot less to talk about. You might even
find it difficult to participate in a lot of the conversations that people have, since
complaining is what they are based around. There is a lot of social bonding that happens
through the victim characters in society. Giving up some of that social connection is
going to be different. That’s going to be okay. You can enjoy your life a lot more, enjoy
those moments a lot more when you break from participating in those patterns. You
might need to get creative in how you connect instead. A good creativity challenge in
communication and expressing your self differently to take on.

Sometimes peace and happiness comes with a price. Sometimes that price is your old
habits.

How is complaining "being right"?

Your Judge has an opinion about something in which it believes it has a superior
approach, method, or answer to how something should be.

“That was a stupid move by that driver.” yes, the driver made a stupid move. However,
are you in the driver’s mind, aware of all they are managing in their life, their day, and
their moment? Have you ever had a lapse in awareness and made a dangerous lane

factors. Perhaps they got off from their shift at the hospital and and are exhausted after
